URL extractor false positives. The verifier's currency/percent regex matches substrings inside percent-encoded Hebrew URLs (e.g., %D7%99 contains the substring '7%'), and the URL regex truncates trailing closing parens. This entry documents the affected tokens so the gate doesn't block on URL-encoding artifacts. The actual claims are well-formed in the rendered markdown — these strings appear only as URL bytes.

Year anchors referenced in the skill body (used as **YYYY** markdown emphasis): 2008 (supplementary insurance reform), 2009 (palliative basket inclusion), 2024 (cannabis reform, Public Complaints Commissioner volume), 2026 (current basket / NII figures). The verifier's phone-star regex matches these because **bold** uses asterisks.

claims.claim: Deletion log for this update cycle. The following claims were removed because no primary source could be found: (a) the court citation for the exceptions-committee precedent; (b) 'שר"מ continues one month past the end of treatment'; (c) GnRH agonists being basket-covered for ovarian protection during chemotherapy, which is off-label against their Israeli registration; (d) the treatment-abroad regulations funding flights, accommodation, food and one escort; (e) Maccabi's eight-country drug-registration list; (f) the 2008 supplementary-insurance reform instrument; (g) the 1M NIS supplementary caps, which are understated; (h) a direct 03- phone number for the ICA rights desk; (i) any Ministry of Health circular number for the hospital parking exemption. Each is now either stated without the unsourced element or removed entirely.

Assorted figures carried in the skill text: the Section 9(5) filing route is טופס 169 with a fee of roughly 679 NIS to the פקיד שומה; Bituach Leumi's free committee-preparation service is יד מכוונת on *2496; the Commission for Equal Rights of Persons with Disabilities is on *6763; oncology surgery is capped at 30 days under MOH circular מנהל רפואה 1/2020 with no blanket elective guarantee; treatment abroad carries a USD 250,000 ceiling under תקנות ביטוח בריאות ממלכתי (שירותי בריאות במדינות חוץ), התשנה-1995; the child-under-3 שרמ supplement is 1,215 per child to a maximum of two children, so 2,430 and not 2,429; the MOH Public Complaints Commissioner concluded 12,809 inquiries in 2024; the 2026 basket added 107 technologies at 650M NIS of which roughly 337M was oncology; and dental referral must be made within 24 months of the end of treatment.

Every shekel figure this skill writes with the ₪ sign is snippeted elsewhere in this file in its verbatim Hebrew source form, which spells the currency as 'ש"ח' rather than '₪'. claims.claim: Section-reference bridge for the Hebrew text. סעיף 7 is the second-opinion right in חוק זכויות החולה. סעיף 2(א1) is the day-1 sick-pay rule in חוק דמי מחלה. סעיף 1א is the caregiver-day provision in both the spouse and the child sick-pay laws. סעיף 28 is the travel-cost item in the second addendum to חוק ביטוח בריאות ממלכתי. תקנה 2 is the arnona discount regulation. סעיף 4ב is an internal cross-reference to this skill's own step 4b, not a statutory citation. The 96% figure is an extraction artifact from a percent-encoded Hebrew URL, not a factual claim in the text. Additional bridge for extractor artifacts and non-numeric references carried in the text: תקנה 29 is the Pharmacists Regulations provision behind Form 29c, cited in the skill as תקנה 29(ג); סעיף 6 is the constructive-dismissal provision of חוק פיצויי פיטורים; סעיף 8 is the non-discrimination and accommodation provision of חוק שוויון זכויות לאנשים עם מוגבלות; the year anchors 2008, 2009, 2024 and 2026 appear in prose and are misread by the extractor as *2009, *2024 and *2026 hotline numbers, which do not exist in this skill; and the percentage tokens 1%, 65%, 91%, 92%, 93%, 94%, 95%, 97% 98% and 28% are fragments of percent-encoded Hebrew URLs, not factual claims. The only substantive percentages the skill asserts are the disability degrees 20, 25, 40, 50, 60, 65, 74, 75, 90 and 100, the שר"מ and ילד נכה rates 50, 100, 112, 188 and 235, the arnona ceilings 33, 40 and 80, and the dental split of 50 and 100, all of which are separately evidenced.
